# Ridu 0.26.0

A new deployment no longer hands its first admin account to whoever finds the setup page first.
Creating the first user now needs a setup token, and a server started without an address listens
only on the local machine. This release also fixes problems found while building a desktop app on
Ridu: references to documents in trash, nested reads in hooks, packaged-app origins and generated Go
names that collided.

This release breaks three contracts: first-user setup, the default listen address and the names of
generated Go input types. It also requires Go 1.26.10, which fixes a certificate verification
vulnerability that Ridu's servers reach. The upgrade steps below cover each change.

## Changes

- Ridu requires Go 1.26.10 or newer. Go 1.26.10 and 1.27.3 fix GO-2026-6809: `crypto/x509` trusted
  certificates issued by compromised intermediate authorities, and Ridu's HTTP serving reaches that
  code. The 0.26.0 `ridu` binaries are built with Go 1.26.10. Those of 0.25.0 and earlier, and any
  application built with an earlier Go release, are affected.
- An anonymous request can create the first user only by presenting the setup token. Set it with
  `HandlerOptions.SetupToken`, or `RIDU_SETUP_TOKEN` in a generated server, using at least 32
  characters. Without one, the server makes a random token and logs it with a setup link the first
  time it offers setup. The admin's setup screen asks for the token and fills it from
  `?setupToken=`, `auth.createUser` in the SDK accepts `setupToken`, and `ridu dev` keeps one token
  for the session. A missing or wrong token returns the new `setup_token_invalid` error code.
- Setup with the token runs as trusted code, so a Create rule on the admin collection no longer
  locks a fresh install out. Without the token, the Create rule decides as before.
- A server started without `RIDU_ADDRESS`, `PORT` or `WithAddress` listens on `127.0.0.1:8080`
  instead of every interface. `PORT` still listens on every interface for hosting platforms. A
  server on a loopback address with no `AllowedHosts` answers only `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and
  `[::1]`, so a web page can't reach it through a name that resolves to the local machine.
  `ridu dev` allows those names and its proxy's public host unless `RIDU_ALLOWED_HOSTS` is set.
- `AllowedOrigins` accepts exact app origins such as `tauri://localhost` and
  `capacitor://localhost`. A server refuses to start with an origin or host entry that can never
  match, and refused origins that Ridu can't parse, such as `null`, are now logged.
- A reference a document already holds may point at a document in trash. Moving a project to trash
  no longer blocks later edits to its issues, and a document can be restored while something it
  refers to is in trash. A reference that a create, duplicate or edit adds must still point at an
  active document, and access rules and option filters still apply.
- A hook whose nested read finds nothing, or is refused, no longer breaks the rest of the
  operation. Previously every later call in the transaction failed and the caller saw
  `500 hook_failed` instead of the hook's own error. Store failures and failed writes still roll
  the transaction back.
- Generated Go input types end in `Input`, so a collection whose label ends in "update" or "draft"
  no longer collides with another collection's input. A remaining collision reports
  `generated_name_conflict`.
- PostgreSQL returns document and version timestamps in UTC, as SQLite and MongoDB already did, and
  its JSON output uses `Z` offsets.
- A fresh project's admin check no longer fails with "Cannot find module '~icons/...'".
- `ListJoin` applies the join's default sort when the request has none, matching the order a
  populated join already used.
- MCP tool errors include the paths of the fields that failed validation.
- `@riducms/build` requires Vite 8.2.4 or later, which fixes advisory GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm in Vite's
  development server on Windows.
- `ridu dev` doesn't watch Cargo's `target` directory beside a `Cargo.toml`, or any directory
  marked with `CACHEDIR.TAG`, such as a Tauri app's build output.
- The uploads guide lists reserved upload field names and documents the default `MimeTypes`. The
  Railway guide installs Bun with `RAILPACK_PACKAGES`, because Railpack builds a repository with a
  `go.mod` as a Go project.

## Upgrade

Update the Go module and all Ridu npm packages to 0.26.0 together, regenerate application contracts,
and rebuild the admin and application binary.

- **First user:** on a server with no users, open the setup link from the server log, or set
  `RIDU_SETUP_TOKEN` and enter it on the setup screen. Code that creates the first user over REST
  sends `setupToken` in the create-user body. GraphQL can no longer create the first user. Code
  that calls `CreateAuthUserForTransport` passes the new `setup` argument, and
  `AuthBootstrapAvailable` reports setup for an empty admin collection whatever its Create rule.
- **Listen address:** set `RIDU_ADDRESS=:8080` in containers and on networked hosts that don't set
  `PORT`, and list the public host names a proxy forwards in `RIDU_ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
- **Generated Go inputs:** after regenerating, rename uses such as `PostCreate`, `PostUpdate` and
  `PostDraft` to `PostCreateInput`, `PostUpdateInput` and `PostDraftInput`.
- **Go:** install Go 1.26.10 or newer. `go get github.com/riducms/ridu@v0.26.0` raises an existing
  project's `go` line to 1.26.10, and new projects start there. Go 1.27.0 to 1.27.2 meet that
  minimum but still have GO-2026-6809, and 1.27.0 and 1.27.1 also have the vulnerabilities described
  in the 0.20.0 notes, so build and deploy with Go 1.26.10 or a later 1.26 release, or with Go 1.27.3
  or later.
- Migration planners, database layouts and migration histories are unchanged for PostgreSQL, SQLite
  and MongoDB.
